entries.subject: Mid-transit time measured from the JWST NIRCam white-light curves (programme 1274)
entries.finding: Torres et al. (2008) give period, a/R*, inclination and radii but no transit time. MAST holds the pipeline's Level 3 white-light curves of two NIRCam grism transits. tools/objects/jwst/fit-transit-time.mts fits a trapezoid with a linear baseline (Nelder-Mead, points over 2000 ppm from a 31-point running median removed) and takes the error from 200 block bootstraps of the residuals. F322W2, 2022-11-11: BJD_TDB 2459893.75120 +/- 0.00005 (4.2 s), depth 1.488%, duration 0.1247 d, residual 503 ppm. F444W, 2022-11-07: 2459890.22649 +/- 0.00005 (4.3 s), depth 1.480%, duration 0.1249 d, residual 646 ppm. The two differ by 3.524706 d, 3.5 s from the published period 3.524746 d and inside their combined error. The F322W2 time is the hosted orbit's phase. A trapezoid has no limb darkening; it is symmetric, so the mid-time does not depend on it, but the depth does and is not used.

entries.subject: Transmission and emission spectra from Hubble and JWST
entries.finding: The planet's atmosphere has been measured in transit by Hubble and JWST. No spectrum gives a surface or a colour, and none is shown. JWST programme 2667 adds a partial MIRI LRS transit (2023). A reduction of the programme 1274 time series has not been attempted.
entries.revisitWhen: When a transmission or emission spectrum is reduced here and a lens that draws it is designed.

entries.subject: Zellem et al. (2014) Spitzer 4.5 um one-sinusoid phase-curve fit, as a map of longitude
entries.finding: Shown as the temperature lens through the Cowan & Agol (2008) inversion. The paper does not say where t = 0 falls in its c1 cos(2 pi t/P) + c2 sin(2 pi t/P); counted from mid-transit, c1 = -0.0410% and c2 = 0.0354% put the peak 40.81 degrees before eclipse and the trough 40.81 degrees before transit, as Table 2 gives both (40.9 +/- 6.0). With the star at the 5,588 K its deeper eclipse (0.1391%) and 1,443 K imply, the curve maximum and minimum give 1,497 and 972 K against Table 3's 1,499 +/- 15 and 972 +/- 44 K. The map runs from 867 K at 139.2 degrees west to 1,557 K at 40.8 degrees east.

entries.subject: Dang et al. (2025) SPCA reanalysis of the same Spitzer 4.5 um phase curve
entries.finding: Offset 43 +5/-6 degrees east, day side 1,420 +/- 20 K, night side 1,010 +70/-80 K (Tables 2 and 3 of arXiv v1): it agrees with the Zellem et al. map, whose transit-time night side is 1,052 K. The paper prints its fluxes, offset and temperatures but not its Fourier coefficients, so its curve cannot be drawn without refitting.
entries.revisitWhen: Its fit coefficients or model curve are published.
